title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp. 14-16. L is a set. A 'figure' F is an admissible family of subsets A ⊂ L (a kind of abstract cell or simplicial complex). Each A has an interior A° and a boundary ∂A. The figures form a set 𝔉(L), partially ordered by ≤ (sub-figure). The support |F| is the union of the members of F. Page 14 introduced the join F⊠G = {A∪B} for figures with disjoint supports, with the Leibniz-type boundary formula ∂(A∪B) = ∂A∪B ∪ A∪∂B.

This page, 'Supports et complément(s)', isolates the orthogonality structure underlying that construction.
(1) Definition. Two figures F, G are disjoint 'in the sense of ≤' (presumably: no common nonzero minorant) iff |F|∩|G| = ∅.
(2) The figures disjoint from every member of a family (G_i) are exactly those with |F| ⊂ L' := L \ ∪|G_i|.
(3) Supports range over arbitrary subsets L' ⊂ L. So the complementation (orthocomplement, or polar) induced by disjointness is just set-theoretic complementation of supports. The lattice of 'bi-orthogonally closed' sets of figures is therefore the Boolean algebra P(L).
(4) The set of figures with support ⊂ L' is identified with 𝔉(L'), the figures on L'. Hence the inclusions 𝔉(L') ⊂ 𝔉(L) are exactly the saturated subsets: downward closed for ≤ and closed for the disjointness polarity.

Purpose: to recover L, and the order and complementation on supports, from the abstract structure (𝔉(L), ≤, disjointness). This is a reconstruction or duality question. Page 16 continues it: with finite families one recovers only the Stone compactification of L (L being its isolated points). This suggests redoing the theory over a totally disconnected compact space X with clopen supports, and over general spaces with pairs of regular open sets (U = int(∁V), V = int(∁U)).
errors: The equivalence 'disjoint in the sense of ≤ ⇔ supports disjoint' tacitly requires that whenever x ∈ |F|∩|G|, there is a nonzero figure (e.g. one supported on {x}) below both. This is not stated on the page.

'Les supports correspondent aux parties quelconques L' de L' is only true if arbitrary (infinite) families are allowed. If figures are finite, supports are finite subsets and their complements are not supports. Page 16 itself acknowledges this by passing to the Stone completion.
Saturation 'au sens de la disjonction' is left vague (trailing '...'). The precise closure operator (the double polar) is not written out.

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures defined via disjointness of supports; the figures orthogonal to a family are those supported in the complement of the union of supports.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality relation / polarity (Galois connection) on a poset; orthogonality space

ideas.what: The bi-orthogonally closed sets of figures form the Boolean algebra of subsets of L. Sub-structures 𝔉(L') ⊂ 𝔉(L) are characterized as the subsets saturated for ≤ and for disjointness.
ideas.modern_name: Lattice of polar-closed sets; restriction to a full subcomplex / sub-space; localization of a complex to a subset of vertices

deep.surprise_reason: A routine bookkeeping page. It sets up an orthogonality/complement structure on figures and identifies figures on a subset with a saturated subset. Standard polarity theory, preparing the Stone-duality remark on p.16. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Title is more likely 'Supports et complément(s)' (image: 'S—ports l co—ff—t'), not 'Supports et composantes'.
The parenthetical '(au sens de ≤)' is written above 'disjoints', followed by '(ssi' rather than 'si'. Read: 'F et G de 𝔉 sont disjoints (au sens de ≤) (ssi |F|∩|G|=∅'.
'la notion de complémentarité est la notion ensembliste'. In the image the connecting word is probably 'est' (or 'et'), and the phrase reads 'la notion ensembliste' rather than a separate clause.
'L'ens. des figures de support ⊂ L'' with the insertion 'de L'' and a struck-out 'et'. This is consistent with the given transcription.
